tests.name: a file's notes, read as the Margin shows them: beside its lines in files_read, among its whys in decisions_for
a package the program imports loads in the run
a run of test files stopped from outside (runs_stop) stops whole, as Ctrl+C stops node --test: the files after it not run
a run's stages are spans: under its run's, the runtime loaded, its entry parsed, its first step — and on its end, what it asked of the editor
a script over the workspace, an agent's: a count across files and what it touched, the network refused, nothing written or outside
a terminal's output, as it printed it
a test file at a commit opened beside the work runs from there: its own modules as that commit has them
a write the policy doesn't decide stops the run and asks; approved, it's made, the run going on from there
checkpoints, as an agent tries a change: noted, changed, a file made, and all of it put back
ESLint's problems as the agents' request has them, each by its rule and place, and each lint a span of ext:eslint's
files: written, read numbered, edited (by text, or by lines), replaced across files or not at all, found, searched (a glob, or a folder's) and deleted
git: a diff of what changed, then the log, a file at a commit and who changed each line
refactoring, as a person does it: where a name's used, renamed everywhere, and a file moved with its imports kept right
search: an extension's findFiles honours its globs; Quick Open and Find in Files find what's there
the bridge: the extension host's one hub, linked to the workbench's, and every debug run's worker linked to it; other extensions only for their records
the debugger, as an agent drives it: Run to a breakpoint, a step, a call's question answered, the Margin read, stopped
the editor as data: the file in front and its tabs, the Problems view, the notifications showing
Trace File Calls: each call at a boundary, for a while — its operation, caller, path and time — as the trace's records
what a preview observed is kept in git too: its page's counts, under the dev server's run, as the server stops
what a run observed is kept in git: its envelope in .silo/runs, each statement's count and each site's values and branches in .silo/evidence
what a way in reaches, as History: What a Way In Reaches… shows it: where it's registered, what only it reaches, who names it
which files BABLR parses, as code_parses asks: each it can't and why, its lines, and asked again from what's kept
every context reports on the architecture plane: the realms, the extensions by their commands, the stores
signing in starts from the GitHub button: pushed to the API, then off to its sign-in page as the editor
the theme follows the system's: VS Code's theme switches, and the shell draws in its colours
